recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No current FHIR-core fix is needed for FHIR-12488; any future behavior change for old R4 maxValueSet extension warnings should be handled as a separate tooling or FHIR-extensions issue.
issue_request: FHIR-12488 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Change Request raised for DSTU2 asking to add a way to indicate elementdefinition-maxValueSet in profile spreadsheets. The Jira application comment says SVN revision 10628 added a max-valueset column to spreadsheet binding tabs and validator support.
initial_application: Git-svn commit 1d0c527ee56ac607a95eb9b65b742e45cea48235, dated 2016-12-23 and titled '#12488 - support for maxValueSet when authoring and validating', changed the DSTU3 validator, IG spreadsheet parser, and a test IG spreadsheet. No prior FHIR-12488 reconciliation commit existed on the combined branch before this worker published d20aa2626e481bfb9c2e469b622a8d706af632aa.
additional_context: The old IG spreadsheet parser/tooling touched by the 2016 application commit is no longer present in the current core checkout. Current build-scope ElementDefinition/profile source expresses the same maximum-binding need through ElementDefinition.binding.additional, including purpose = maximum and additional.valueSet. The terminology page states that maximum additional bindings replace the elementdefinition-maxValueSet extension in FHIR Release 5+, and the FHIR Extension Pack carries the legacy extension as retired/deprecated with guidance to use additionalBinding instead.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. Reintroducing or documenting the historical max-valueset spreadsheet column in current FHIR core would be stale because the DSTU2/STU3 spreadsheet workflow was already served and current R5/R6 source uses first-class additional bindings plus deprecated extension-pack compatibility.
